note: E1; E3: FY2025 water consumption fell from 281 ML to 250 ML (about 11%), so overall water consumption improved in the deadline year; E6 renews the aim for FY2026 but does not undo the FY2025 result.

E6; E8-E9: the FY2024 report restates the 15-event target and says it was surpassed with over 80 CSR activities in FY2024 ('participated in' rather than 'conducted', but the company counts them against this target); E12 shows the same in FY2025.

E5-E7: in 2025 the company 'has started to install' the biocarbon plant at United Winery Distillery and E7 gives its savings in the future tense; installation in progress, no completion reported. E4's 'completed in 2026' belongs to the Myanmar bioenergy boiler of E3, not this plant.

E5; E8: the FY2024 report says the Scope 3 inventory was completed that year, fully deriving all material categories (seven disclosed), and target-setting exploration begins next; E1 lists the FY2024 Scope 3 result as met. E10/E12 repeat the same 'this year' wording in 2025, which reads as carried-over text.

E2-E3; E9; E12: the 2024 report moves the all-KUD ISPO target to 2026 (a moved deadline); in 2025 only four KUD are certified with one more mid-audit (E6 implies at least ten KUD), and E12 re-ties the target to the national mandatory timeline.

E3; E7; E5; E11-E12: a qualitative scenario analysis was conducted (reported 2024 and 2025), but the company still 'remains committed to scenario analysis' and defers the quantitative analysis to coming years. The promise and extraction carry neither qualifier, so I cannot tell whether the qualitative exercise is the promised analysis or a partial step; case worth writing up.

E7; E10: the 2023 report says even the narrowed aim (substitution testing for three of the remaining eight industrial products by end-2023) was delayed, with full substitution still only a commitment; the 2024 report is still trialling a new formulation.

E4; E8; E10-E11: the evidence frames the target as carbon emission intensity from a 2020 baseline, qualifiers missing from the extraction. E4's 'not achieved on time' sits in a flattened row that also holds the energy-intensity target and its 22.5% remark, so it cannot be attributed to the emission target; E10's 32% cut is absolute Scope 1+2, not intensity, a related measure rather than this target.

E8-E9: the 2025 report states the five-year 50% waste reduction target was not met and delayed. The evidence specifies waste intensity (sludge and rubber lump per 1,000 pieces, 2020 baseline), omitted from the extraction, but it is the company's only waste target so the verdict is this target's.
E5; E7; E9: FY2022 average training hours were 13.0 per employee and the report says the 10-hour goal was surpassed; E12's later 15-hour target is a new, higher goal, not a retreat on this one.
